disagreements.position: Severity should be raised from P3 to P1, not left as a hygiene/webhook-routing item.
disagreements.evidence: RazorpayWebhookController.java:167-176 states the shared account is a 'fixed constraint, not a migration' because separating it 'would mean separating the legal entities.' Read together with EV-007/TEJAS-01 (the live copy promises brand funds are held by a dedicated licensed Payment Aggregator and 'never pooled in Influora's own bank account'), a merchant settlement account that is *also* used by an unrelated product (Snapsby) is a second, independent way that custody claim is false -- it is not just an engineering webhook-dispatch nuance, it is evidence there is no dedicated, segregated financial relationship for Campaign funds at all. It also creates an audit/reconciliation exposure: Influora's own P&L and any future RBI PA-licensing application would need to defend commingled settlement with another business's revenue.

missed_issues.title: The flagship payment-trust marketing page (secure-payments.tsx) is the one page missing the team's own banned-phrase governance comment, and independently makes an unconditional 'Guaranteed payment' claim to creators that EV-015's code path falsifies
missed_issues.evidence: src/pages/features/secure-payments.tsx (the page 'was /features/escrow -- renamed in T-SEOCRO-0819', per its own top-of-file comment at lines 4-6) contains no banned-phrase/governance comment block at all. By contrast, three sibling marketing pages that carry the same class of payment-custody claims each have one: src/pages/features/hype.tsx:41-49 ('"escrow" is banned in user copy (2026-09-02)... "Bank-Grade 256-Bit Rails". No security/certification claims about Influora... None of this is measured'), src/pages/features/deal-room.tsx:45, and src/pages/how-it-works-brands.tsx:43,446 (same 2026-09-02 ruling, 'escrow is also banned', '"Active Escrow Contracts" (banned vocabulary)'). secure-payments.tsx:36 nonetheless reads: "Guaranteed payment. The brand's money is already locked and protected before you film a single reel..." -- an unconditional guarantee to creators. That guarantee is directly contradicted by EscrowService.java:946-988's refund(principal, workspaceId, escrowHoldId), which lets a brand OWNER/ADMIN refund a FUNDED hold on demand (status check is EscrowStatus.FUNDED only, no delivery/approval/dispute precondition -- confirmed by the code's own comment ~line 898 that the dispute check is deliberately withheld from this path, matching EV-015). It is also undercut by EV-002's double-fund/release-integrity findings on the same FUNDED state.
missed_issues.location: src/pages/features/secure-payments.tsx:4-6 (missing governance header), :36 ('Guaranteed payment' claim); cross-referenced against influora-api/src/main/java/com/influora/service/EscrowService.java:898,946-988 (refund path) and EV-002/EV-015 in merged-register.json
missed_issues.impact: This is the single highest financial-trust page on the marketing surface for creators (the audience with the least leverage to chase a brand that pulls funds back). An absolute 'guaranteed' promise that the platform's own code can void unilaterally is a direct consumer-claims liability (ASCI/consumer-protection exposure, the same category the team already treats seriously per the removed-fabricated-stats precedent tejas.json cites), and it slipped through precisely because this page -- alone among its siblings -- has no banned-phrase review comment to have caught it.
missed_issues.recommended_fix: 1) Add the same governance/banned-phrase comment block used in hype.tsx/deal-room.tsx/how-it-works-brands.tsx to secure-payments.tsx and re-audit its full copy against that list (it also repeats the 'licensed, RBI-authorized Payment Aggregator' claim at lines 97 and 210 per tejas.json's citation). 2) Replace the unconditional 'Guaranteed payment' line with language conditioned on delivery/approval and disclosing the dispute/refund path, consistent with terms-of-service.md:28's own 'we do not guarantee ... outcome' facilitator disclaimer. 3) Treat EV-015's fix (gating brand-initiated refund behind delivery/approval or dispute state) as a prerequisite for this copy claim being true at all, not just a security fix.
missed_issues.verification_required: After the copy and code fixes, re-grep all marketing pages for the string 'guarant' and confirm each hit either has a conditioning clause or a governance-comment exemption; add a CI/lint check (or an extension of the existing citations.rc proof-os gate) that fails if a new feature page under src/pages/features/ lacks the banned-phrase comment block that its siblings carry.
